AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To evaluate the provision of procedural sedation during abortion by expert nurses and to describe the factors that are associated with time to discharge for women who receive this sedation.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Descriptive statistics were generated to describe a retrospective cohort of women presenting for abortion under procedural sedation. Analysis of variance was used to determine significant characteristics that influenced time to discharge.

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: A single clinical site that employs seven expert nurses.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: A total of 194 medical records were available for this analysis.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: All women were discharged home with accompaniment, and no incidents of respiratory distress or other adverse complications occurred. Most women (n = 136) received at least 150 μg fentanyl and 3 mg midazolam, and 71% of women in the first trimester and 83% of women in the second trimester entered the recovery area with no pain. Variables significantly associated with time spent in the recovery area were gestational age at time of abortion (t = -2.68, p = .008), pain at entry to recovery area (t = -0.254, p = .008), and pain at 15 minutes (t = 0.25, p = .038).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Expert nurses can administer procedural sedation for pain control associated with abortion and are capable of monitoring women and helping them return to baseline status after the procedure.

Article.ArticleTitle: Retrospective Evaluation of the Procedural Sedation Practices of Expert Nurses During Abortion Care.

Journal.Title: Journal of obstetric, gynecologic, and neonatal nursing : JOGNN
